questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: Free gas under the diaphragm on an erect chest radiograph indicates:
questions.concept: Pneumoperitoneum is best seen on an erect chest film or left lateral decubitus, and in a patient with an acute abdomen indicates perforation, most often of a duodenal ulcer, requiring urgent surgery.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: Multiple air-fluid levels with dilated central small bowel loops showing valvulae conniventes indicate:
questions.concept: Valvulae conniventes cross the full bowel width and the loops lie centrally, unlike colonic haustra which cross only part of the lumen with peripheral loops. More than three air-fluid levels suggests obstruction.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: The investigation of choice for suspected acute appendicitis in a young adult male is:
questions.concept: CT has high sensitivity and specificity showing a thickened appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding. Ultrasound is preferred first in children and pregnancy to avoid radiation, and MRI in pregnancy if ultrasound is inconclusive.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: The imaging investigation of choice for gallstones is:
questions.concept: Ultrasound detects over 95% of gallstones as mobile echogenic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing, and also shows wall thickening and duct dilatation. Only about 10 to 15% of gallstones are radio-opaque on plain film.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: A coffee-bean sign on abdominal radiograph indicates:
questions.concept: A massively dilated closed loop arising from the pelvis with apposed medial walls forms the coffee-bean or omega sign. Caecal volvulus instead displaces the dilated loop towards the left upper quadrant.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: A string sign of Kantor on barium study of the terminal ileum suggests:
questions.concept: Narrowing of the terminal ileal lumen from oedema and fibrosis produces a thin barium stream. Cobblestoning, skip lesions and fistulae are other Crohn features; ileocaecal tuberculosis is the main differential in India.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: The target or doughnut sign on abdominal ultrasound in an infant indicates:
questions.concept: Concentric rings of invaginated bowel produce a target sign in transverse and pseudokidney in longitudinal section. Ultrasound is the investigation of choice, avoiding radiation, and guides pneumatic reduction.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: MRCP is preferred over ERCP for biliary imaging because it:
options: Is non-invasive and avoids the risk of post-procedure pancreatitis
questions.concept: MRCP is purely diagnostic with no risk of pancreatitis, bleeding or perforation, so ERCP is now reserved for cases needing intervention such as stone extraction, stenting or sphincterotomy.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: Rigler sign on a supine abdominal radiograph refers to:
options: Visualisation of both sides of the bowel wall due to free intraperitoneal gas
questions.concept: Air on both the luminal and peritoneal surfaces outlines the wall, indicating pneumoperitoneum on a supine film where free gas under the diaphragm cannot be assessed. The football sign is a large midline gas collection.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Abdominal & GIT imaging; acute abdomen signs
questions.stem: Gas in the biliary tree (pneumobilia) with small bowel obstruction and an ectopic gallstone constitutes:
questions.concept: A large gallstone erodes through a cholecystoduodenal fistula and impacts at the terminal ileum. Rigler triad of pneumobilia, obstruction and an ectopic calcified stone is diagnostic.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Abdominal Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: The most accurate ultrasound parameter for dating a pregnancy in the first trimester is:
questions.concept: Crown-rump length between 7 and 13 weeks dates pregnancy to within about 5 days because early growth is highly uniform; accuracy declines progressively with advancing gestation.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Obstetric Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: The anomaly scan in pregnancy is optimally performed at:
questions.concept: By 18 to 20 weeks organogenesis is complete and fetal size permits detailed structural assessment, while still allowing time for further investigation and decision-making within legal limits for termination.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Obstetric Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: The mammographic finding most suspicious of malignancy is:
options: Clustered pleomorphic branching microcalcification with a spiculated mass
questions.concept: Fine pleomorphic linear branching microcalcifications suggest ductal carcinoma in situ, and a spiculated mass with architectural distortion suggests invasive carcinoma. Popcorn calcification indicates an involuting fibroadenoma.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Breast Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: The imaging modality of choice for a breast lump in a woman under 35 years is:
questions.concept: Dense fibroglandular tissue in younger women limits mammographic sensitivity, so ultrasound is preferred and reliably distinguishes cystic from solid lesions. Mammography is the screening tool above 40.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Breast Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: The BI-RADS classification is used to:
options: Standardise reporting and management recommendations for breast imaging
questions.concept: BI-RADS categories run from 0 (incomplete) through 1 and 2 (normal or benign) to 5 (highly suggestive of malignancy) and 6 (biopsy-proven), each with a defined management recommendation.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Breast Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: A snowstorm appearance of the uterine cavity with no fetal parts indicates:
questions.concept: Hydropic villi produce multiple small cystic spaces giving the snowstorm or cluster-of-grapes pattern, usually with a uterus large for dates, very high hCG and bilateral theca lutein cysts.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Obstetric Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: Transvaginal ultrasound is preferred over transabdominal in early pregnancy because it:
options: Gives higher resolution allowing earlier detection of the gestational sac and cardiac activity
questions.concept: The higher frequency probe placed close to the pelvic organs improves resolution, detecting an intrauterine sac from about 4.5 to 5 weeks and cardiac activity from 6 weeks - crucial in suspected ectopic pregnancy.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Obstetric Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: The most reliable ultrasound sign of ectopic pregnancy is:
options: An adnexal mass with an extrauterine gestational sac containing a yolk sac or embryo
questions.concept: Definitive diagnosis requires visualising an extrauterine sac, though this is uncommon; more often an empty uterus with beta-hCG above the discriminatory zone, an adnexal mass and free fluid raise suspicion.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Obstetric Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: In the PC-PNDT Act context, ultrasound in pregnancy must not be used to:
options: Determine or disclose the sex of the fetus
questions.concept: The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act prohibits sex determination and disclosure to combat female foeticide; registration of clinics, record maintenance and prominent display of notices are mandatory.
questions.reference: Park 27e, PC-PNDT Act

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Obstetric, breast & pelvic imaging
questions.stem: Hysterosalpingography is best performed:
options: In the follicular phase, days 7 to 10, after menstruation has ceased
questions.concept: Performing it after bleeding stops but before ovulation avoids disturbing an early pregnancy and gives a clean cavity for assessment. It is contraindicated in active pelvic infection and pregnancy.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Gynaecological Imaging

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: The radionuclide most widely used in diagnostic nuclear medicine is:
questions.concept: Technetium-99m has a 6-hour half-life and emits pure gamma radiation at 140 keV, ideal for imaging with minimal patient dose, and is available from a portable molybdenum-99 generator.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Nuclear Medicine

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: A bone scan using technetium-99m MDP shows increased uptake in all EXCEPT:
questions.concept: Bone scans detect osteoblastic activity, so purely lytic myeloma lesions are typically cold or normal, which is why skeletal survey or whole-body MRI is preferred for myeloma staging.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Nuclear Medicine

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: Iodine-131 is used therapeutically in thyroid disease because it emits:
options: Beta particles causing local tissue destruction, with gamma emission allowing imaging
questions.concept: Beta emission destroys thyroid tissue over a short range, treating thyrotoxicosis and thyroid carcinoma, while the gamma component permits scanning. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Nuclear Medicine

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: FDG-PET detects tumours by exploiting their:
questions.concept: Fluorodeoxyglucose accumulates in metabolically active cells reflecting the Warburg effect, making PET valuable for staging, detecting recurrence and assessing treatment response, usually fused with CT for localisation.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Nuclear Medicine

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: Brachytherapy differs from teletherapy in that the radiation source is:
options: Placed within or adjacent to the tumour
At a distance from the patient
questions.concept: Brachytherapy delivers a very high local dose with rapid fall-off by the inverse square law, sparing surrounding tissue, and is central to treating carcinoma cervix. Teletherapy uses an external beam at a distance.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Radiotherapy

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: The most radiosensitive cells in the body are:
options: Rapidly dividing cells such as bone marrow, gonads and intestinal mucosa
questions.concept: By the law of Bergonie and Tribondeau, radiosensitivity increases with mitotic activity and decreases with differentiation, which explains both radiotherapy toxicity and the effectiveness of fractionation.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Radiotherapy

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: Fractionation in radiotherapy is used to:
options: Allow normal tissue repair and tumour reoxygenation between doses
questions.concept: Dividing the total dose exploits differences between tumour and normal tissue in the four Rs - repair, redistribution, repopulation and reoxygenation - improving the therapeutic ratio.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Radiotherapy

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is indicated for:
options: Refractory variceal bleeding or ascites in portal hypertension
questions.concept: TIPS creates a low-resistance channel between the portal and hepatic veins, decompressing varices. Its main complication is hepatic encephalopathy from diverting portal blood away from the liver.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Interventional Radiology

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: Uterine artery embolisation is an established alternative to surgery for:
options: Symptomatic uterine fibroids and intractable postpartum haemorrhage
questions.concept: Embolising both uterine arteries causes fibroid infarction with symptom relief while preserving the uterus, and is life-saving in postpartum haemorrhage where fertility is to be conserved.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Interventional Radiology

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.topic: Nuclear medicine, radiotherapy basics & interventional radiology
questions.stem: The ALARA principle in radiation protection stands for:
questions.concept: ALARA underpins justification, optimisation and dose limitation - the three pillars of radiation protection - implemented through shielding, distance, time minimisation and avoiding unnecessary investigations.
questions.reference: Sutton's Textbook of Radiology 8e, Radiation Protection
